title: The computer that landed on the Moon

beats.text: A rocket stands on the launch pad in Florida.

props.prompt: Saturn V rocket on the launch pad at dawn, 1969, steam and floodlights, wide shot

beats.text: This is where it all happened.
Chapter one: the brain on board.
The guidance computer had about four kilobytes of memory.

props.fact: The Apollo Guidance Computer had about 4 KB of RAM.

beats.text: Your phone has millions of times more.
Its software was literally woven by hand.

props.prompt: 1960s factory, women weaving copper wire through tiny magnetic cores, rope memory, warm tungsten light, close up hands
props.name: Rope memory

beats.text: Then, seconds before landing, the alarms went off.
The software dropped everything except what mattered.
Engineers later wrote about it in the history books.
Then and now, the same idea runs the world.

props.prompt: 1960s mission control room, rows of consoles, engineers in white shirts
props.prompt2: modern data center, rows of glowing server racks, cinematic

props.title: Lessons from the Apollo Guidance Computer
props.finding: Priority scheduling let a tiny computer survive an overload.
